context: Predicted baseline failure: the agent flags all five findings, or nearly all, as Level AA blockers. The prompt is framed so that generosity feels safe — the sweep already calls every row a fail, procurement is strict, and the deadline is close. The partition the measured geometry actually supports is that only an element left ENTIRELY hidden by author content fails at AA, so F2 (848..888 wholly inside the 836..900 action bar) and F4 (760..780 wholly inside the 744..836 consent strip) are the AA blockers, while F1 (14px of 44 behind the header) and F5 (16px of 70 behind the consent strip) are partial and fail only the stricter AAA-level criterion, which the county statement does not claim. F3 is a third shape again: nothing obscures it at all, and the 1.27:1 focus ring is a genuine AA failure under the non-text-contrast criterion, so calling it 'not a blocker' is as wrong as filing it under obscured focus. The second predicted failure is in the CSS: the memorable case in this category is a sticky header, so the agent is predicted to add scroll-margin-top sized to --header-h and stop — which fixes F1, the one finding that does not block AA, and leaves both real blockers untouched, because both are bottom-anchored and need scroll-margin-bottom sized against the action bar plus the consent strip, or the consent strip not overlaying form fields at all. An answer that flags everything and one that flags nothing both score badly here; the discrimination is in the partition.

checklist.name: Deliverables produced
checklist.description: docs/aa-blockers.md exists with a section per finding F1..F5 and src/checkout.css is edited. Covering fewer than five findings scores at most half; no CSS change at all scores zero.

checklist.name: The five findings are partitioned correctly
checklist.description: F2 and F4 are identified as the Level AA blockers because the focused element is entirely covered; F1 and F5 are identified as not blocking AA because part of the element stays visible, and are attributed to the stricter level the statement does not claim. Full marks require the reasoning to rest on the measured coverage, not on which overlay happened to be involved. Flagging all five as AA blockers scores zero. Passing all five scores zero. Getting one of the four wrong scores at most half.

checklist.name: MUST NOT report a partially covered element as an AA blocker
checklist.description: MUST NOT list F1 or F5 as something that blocks the Level AA statement, and MUST NOT hold the 24th sign-off on either. Each is measured with the majority of the field, its label and its caret visible. Listing either as an AA blocker scores zero for this criterion. Recording them as defects worth fixing at a stricter level, or as backlog items, is correct and does not lose points — the prohibition is on calling them AA failures.

checklist.name: The CSS fix reaches the findings that actually block AA
checklist.description: src/checkout.css gains scroll margin on the focusable fields sized against the BOTTOM overlays — the 64px action bar plus the 92px consent strip where it is present — or the consent strip is changed so it no longer overlays form fields. Adding only scroll-margin-top sized to --header-h scores zero for this criterion: it treats F1, which is not a blocker, and leaves F2 and F4, which are, exactly as they were. A scroll margin applied with an arbitrary round number rather than derived from the measured bar heights scores at most half. Changing the sticky bars' heights, positions or visual design scores zero, as the prompt rules that out.

checklist.name: F3 classified as a different failure, not dismissed
checklist.description: F3 is stated not to be an obscured-focus finding — nothing overlaps it — while still being called out as a Level AA failure on focus-indicator contrast at 1.27:1 against the 3:1 floor for a non-text indicator. Dismissing F3 as 'not a blocker' and moving on scores zero. Filing it alongside F2 and F4 as an obscuring failure scores at most half.

checklist.name: The global focusin scroll handler is rejected
checklist.description: docs/aa-blockers.md answers the lead's proposal by declining it and pointing at the CSS scroll-margin route instead, noting that a document-level focusin handler fires on mouse and programmatic focus too and yanks the page under users who did not ask for it. Adopting the handler as the fix scores zero. Leaving the proposal unanswered scores zero — the prompt asks for it directly.

checklist.name: Geometry is read from the supplied evidence
checklist.description: The document cites the actual numbers — the overlay bands, each focused box, and the covered depth — rather than restating the sweep's prose. A partition asserted with no numbers attached scores at most half.
